title: Compute Options for Developers
description: Get a high-level overview of the main Azure compute services developers use to run applications.

data.text: Azure offers several ways to run your code, each with different levels of control and convenience. As a developer, you usually choose between Virtual Machines, App Service, Functions, or Container Apps depending on what you are building.

In cloud terms, compute is the brain power that runs your application. It is the CPU and memory behind your web API, background job, or website. Azure provides four main compute services for developers.

data.title: The Four Main Options
items: **Virtual Machines (VMs)** — You get a full Windows or Linux server in the cloud. You manage the operating system, patches, and runtime. Best when you need maximum control.
**App Service** — A managed platform for web apps, APIs, and mobile backends. Azure handles the infrastructure; you focus on code. The most common choice for web developers.
**Azure Functions** — Serverless functions that run only when triggered. Great for small pieces of logic, file processing, or event-driven tasks. You pay only while code is running.
**Container Apps** — Run containerized microservices without managing Kubernetes yourself. Good when your app is already packaged in Docker.

data.title: Azure Compute Options at a Glance

cards.title: Virtual Machines
cards.description: Full control over a cloud-hosted server.
cons: You patch and update the OS

cards.title: App Service
cards.description: Managed hosting for web apps and APIs.

terms.definition: The CPU and memory resources that run your application code in the cloud.
A software emulation of a physical computer, giving you full control over the operating system.
The set of compute resources (CPU, memory) that power one or more App Service apps.
A cloud model where you write code without thinking about servers; the platform automatically allocates resources.
A lightweight, portable package that includes an app and all its dependencies.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure compute is the CPU and memory that runs your app in the cloud.
VMs give you full control; App Service and Functions give you less overhead.
App Service is the default choice for most web APIs and front-end apps.
Functions work best for event-driven or sporadic workloads.
Container Apps are ideal when your app already runs in Docker.
data.takeaway: Start with App Service for most web apps; move to Functions or Containers only when you have a clear reason.
